items.title: Lebrel Brings Uncensored DeepSeek V4.1 Flash From $0.13 per Million Input Tokens, Adds Alibaba's Qwen4-Max on Day One
items.summary_1line: Lebrel Brings Uncensored DeepSeek V4.1 Flash From $0.13 per Million Input Tokens, Adds Alibaba's Qwen4-Max on Day One markets.businessinsider.com
items.editor_note: Adds a hosted price point and a modified "uncensored" variant from a third-party provider.

editorial.tldr: This thread is now a pattern across independent third parties running DeepSeek V4 and V4.1 Flash outside DeepSeek's own API, not one event. It began Oct 29 with Rival.io's GraphX claiming Flash serving on eight NVIDIA L4 GPUs, then a lawyer's private server build on Nov 14 fit 80% of V4.1 Flash on an eight-V100 server at 4-bit NVFP4.
editorial.whats_new: Hosting provider Lebrel added an uncensored DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on Nov 18 from $0.13 per million input tokens, alongside Alibaba's Qwen4-Max on day one.
editorial.why_it_matters: Flash is spreading to third-party hosts and modest self-hosted hardware, so price and footprint options are widening while each provider's model variant, safety tuning and performance stay unverified.
editorial.take_for_builders: Before routing traffic to a third-party Flash host, confirm which checkpoint and safety tuning it serves and rerun your evals on it; treat the L4 and V100 footprints as unbenchmarked until throughput data appears.
